elements.requirement: The statutory principles set out in this provision apply for all purposes of the Mental Capacity Act 2005.
elements.quote: The following principles apply for the purposes of this Act.

elements.requirement: A person must be assumed to possess mental capacity unless it is established that the person lacks capacity.
elements.quote: A person must be assumed to have capacity unless it is established that he lacks capacity.

elements.requirement: A person must not be treated as unable to make a decision unless all practicable steps to assist that person in making the decision have been taken without success.
elements.quote: A person is not to be treated as unable to make a decision unless all practicable steps to help him to do so have been taken without success.

elements.requirement: A person must not be treated as unable to make a decision solely because that person makes an unwise decision.
elements.quote: A person is not to be treated as unable to make a decision merely because he makes an unwise decision.

elements.requirement: Any act carried out or decision made under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 for or on behalf of an individual who lacks capacity must be carried out or made in that individual's best interests.
elements.quote: An act done, or decision made, under this Act for or on behalf of a person who lacks capacity must be done, or made, in his best interests.

elements.requirement: Before an act is done or a decision is made under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 on behalf of an individual lacking capacity, consideration must be given to whether the underlying purpose can be achieved as effectively through a measure that is less restrictive of that individual's rights and freedom of action.
elements.quote: Before the act is done, or the decision is made, regard must be had to whether the purpose for which it is needed can be as effectively achieved in a way that is less restrictive of the person's rights and freedom of action.
